new_roadmap:
Read AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md,
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md, cpm.project.json, and applicable .cursor/rules.

Do not implement code.

Create/refine TODO.md as small, independently verifiable phases.
For every phase include goal, expected files/components, acceptance criteria,
focused verification, and stop conditions.

Include tests alongside behavior.
Include security and production-readiness work where relevant.
Do not commit or push.
build_phase:
Read AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md,
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md, TODO.md, cpm.project.json, and applicable .cursor/rules.

Implement ONLY the current approved TODO phase: {{phase}}.

Before editing inspect related code, identify reuse, list expected changed files,
and identify compatibility/security risk.

During implementation:
- keep the diff scoped;
- do not implement later phases;
- do not introduce parallel architecture;
- add/update tests with behavior;
- do not weaken valid tests;
- do not hardcode credentials.

After implementation run focused verification, the project verification command,
and inspect git diff.

If the work requires an unplanned architecture, schema, public contract,
or security-boundary change, STOP and report it.

Do not commit or push.
existing_discovery:
Do not modify files.

Requested change: {{idea}}

Trace the relevant subsystem using repository evidence:
entry points, routes/handlers, services, persistence/state, schemas/types,
authentication, authorization, jobs/events, integrations, configuration,
tests, callers, and downstream dependencies.

Explain runtime flow from input to final outcome.

Separate:
A. verified behavior
B. inference
C. unknowns

Identify existing patterns a compatible change must preserve.

Do not redesign, edit, commit, or push.
existing_agents:
You are onboarding Cursor into an existing repository.

Read repository evidence, BASELINE_AUDIT.md, existing AGENTS.md if present,
and existing .cursor/rules.

Do NOT implement the requested feature.

Create/refine AGENTS.md so it describes the system that ACTUALLY exists:
important directories, verified architecture patterns, real verification commands,
minimal-blast-radius expectations, verified security/data boundaries,
Git authority, stop conditions, and verified do-not-touch areas.

Do not encode guesses as facts.
Preserve stronger existing instructions.
Do not commit or push.
blast_radius:
Requested change:
{{idea}}

Do not modify code.

Create/refine CHANGE_PLAN.md using repository evidence.

Identify exact modules, callers, downstream dependencies, database/state impact,
API/event impact, auth/authz impact, infrastructure/UI impact,
compatibility/migration/concurrency risk, edge cases, existing tests,
and required regression tests.

Classify:
MUST CHANGE
MAY CHANGE
MUST NOT CHANGE

Propose the smallest compatible implementation, verification, and rollback.

Do not code, commit, or push.
existing_implement:
Read AGENTS.md, BASELINE_AUDIT.md, CHANGE_PLAN.md,
relevant docs, and applicable .cursor/rules.

Implement ONLY the approved change:
{{idea}}

Preserve architecture, minimize blast radius, avoid unrelated cleanup,
reuse existing abstractions, preserve compatibility unless approved otherwise,
add regression tests, preserve authorization/data boundaries,
and do not weaken valid checks.

Run focused verification and the full regression plan.

If an existing contract conflicts with the request, STOP and report it.

Do not commit or push.
security_review:
Perform a security review of the completed project/change.

Review external input/validation, authentication, authorization/data ownership,
sensitive data/logging, secrets, dependencies, subprocess/shell execution,
injection/SSRF/deserialization where relevant, GitHub Actions permissions/pins,
infrastructure/IAM, migrations/destructive behavior, and project-specific
security requirements from cpm.project.json.

Use deterministic security tools where configured.

Separate verified findings, manual-review risks, and accepted/irrelevant findings.
Do not claim a passing scan proves the project is secure.
Do not commit or push.
